entries.title: The day-after midterm rally that fades (the 2018 script)

when.summary: A midterm year, from election day through year end.

point_out: Stocks ripped the day after the 2018 midterms, then gave it all back and fell into Christmas Eve.
Now look at this year: up on Wednesday, then all of it gone and more on Thursday. 2018 took 4 sessions to do that. This took 1.
In 2018, Bitcoin had already made its February low and its June low, and it felt like things would hold. Then stocks broke and took it down.

numbers.text: 2018: S&P closed 2,755.45 on election day, +2.12% the next day, first close back under the election close on Nov 12 (4 sessions later), low 2,351.10 on Dec 24, -14.67% from the election close and -19.8% from the Sept 20 peak
2026: S&P closed 7,568.92 on election day, +1.58% on Nov 4, then -4.36% on Nov 5 to 7,353.73, already -2.84% from the election close
Up the day after and still below the election close at year end happened in 4 of the 19 midterms from 1950 to 2022: 1966, 1986, 2002, 2018

entries.mike_angle: Same picture, different cause. The calendar did not do this, a hiking Fed and an AI crash did. You are not a four-year cycle zombie, so you get to show the chart and still reject the cycle explanation.
careful: One precedent is an analogy, not a rule. Only 4 of 19 midterms did this.
Pair it with midterm-12-months-later so the video does not read as a blanket bear call.

entries.title: Every midterm since 1950: higher 12 months later

when.summary: A midterm year, from election day through year end. The counterweight to the 2018 fade.

point_out: 19 midterms since 1950. The S&P was higher 12 months after election day in all 19.
Even 2018. It fell almost 15% first and was still up 11.7% a year later.
So the people saying sell the midterm and the people saying buy it can both be right, it depends on your time frame.

numbers.text: S&P 12 months after the election-day close, 1950 to 2022: higher 19 of 19, median +14.5%, smallest +1.1% (1986), 2018 +11.7%
S&P from the election-day close to Dec 31: higher 13 of 19, median +2.41%

entries.mike_angle: This is the macro version of being bullish the next year without believing in a four-year cycle. It is a stocks statistic, so say that plainly before you connect it to crypto.
careful: 19 for 19 is a small sample that never included a Fed hiking into a Nasdaq correction with oil near 100. It is a tendency, not a law.
sources: Our own study from S&P daily closes (scripts/market_data.py). Heresy Financial's 'This Happens After Every Midterms' (105.9K views at 3 days) shows there is an audience for it: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j4f3ulJA12E

entries.title: The Fed keeps hiking while stocks fall (and how 2018 ended)

when.summary: The Fed's most recent move was a hike in the last 6 months, and the S&P is at least 5% off its high.

point_out: 2018: hike in September, skip November, hike in December, while the market was falling. Same sequence so far in 2026: hike in September, hold in October, December live.
2018 ended when the Fed blinked. Dec 19 projections still showed 2 more hikes for 2019, Powell shifted on Jan 4, the S&P jumped 3.43% that day, and the Fed never hiked in 2019. It cut 3 times.
Here's the thing about that 2018 comparison: M2 was growing 3.2% then. It is growing 5.7% now. Nearly double.

numbers.text: Fed target upper bound moves: 2018 to 2.25 on Sep 27 and 2.50 on Dec 20 (effective dates); none up in 2019, cuts on Aug 1, Sep 19, Oct 31 2019; 2026 up to 4.00 on Sep 17
Oct 28 2026: held at 3.75% to 4%, Cook and Hammack dissented in favor of a hike
CME FedWatch: 70.1% for a December hike, down from 82.7% on Wednesday and 79.9% a week earlier (live-drift, re-read before recording)

Dec 2018 projections showed two more hikes for 2019; Powell's Oct 3 2018 line: 'We're a long way from neutral now, probably'; Jan 4 2019 Q&A at the American Economic Association: 'always prepared to shift the stance of policy'
M2 year over year: 3.17% in Nov 2018, 5.71% in Sept 2026, the latest month
numbers.basis: computed: FRED M2SL, monthly, seasonally adjusted

entries.mike_angle: This is your macro-liquidity thesis applied to the 2018 chart. If liquidity is the real driver, 2026 is not 2018, because M2 is growing at nearly double the pace.
careful: 'Patient' belongs to the January 2019 statement, not the Jan 4 Q&A. M2 growth is a nominal figure and inflation is elevated, so expect pushback in the comments.
